productContext.title: Where it all started
description: I didn't begin my journey as a software engineer.
I started as someone who was always curious about how things worked — how individual parts connect, how systems behave, and how ideas become something tangible.

My academic background was in Mechanical Engineering, where I learned to approach problems from a systems perspective: breaking complex challenges into smaller components, understanding the relationship between them, and designing solutions that work together.
But along the way, I discovered another kind of engineering — one where ideas could be transformed into experiences through code.
Software gave me the ability to experiment, create, and bring concepts to life faster than I had imagined.
That curiosity became the first step in my transition from designing physical systems to building digital ones.

aboutContext.title: Learning to build
description: My first real introduction to programming came through The Odin Project — a platform built around one simple idea: learn by building.
What fascinated me was not just learning how websites worked, but the process behind creating them.
A website was no longer just something I used every day; it became something I could understand, deconstruct, and eventually build myself.
Driven by curiosity, I started exploring the foundations of web development:
Experimenting, breaking things, and finding solutions
The early projects were simple, but each one taught me something new.
Every feature I built became a new challenge.
Every bug I fixed became a lesson.
And slowly, writing code became more than learning a skill — it became a way of thinking.

role: Owned frontend architecture and UI systems
Built real-time features and collaborative workflows
Worked closely with backend and product teams

projects.title: Email Editor
projects.problem: Users needed a Gmail-like editor with drafts, templates, and previews.
projects.solution: Built a modular email editor using Tiptap with autosave, signatures, previews, and export support.

learnings: Modular UI systems scale better than page-level design
State architecture impacts performance more than rendering
